_about: Raw reports behind docs/research/2026-10-02-windows-port-estimate.md: five audits (build tool, engine C++, script host, dependencies and scripts, WSL2), the combined phased plan, and a skeptical review of it. Read-only audits at 60b757ee..edbfe1b1; nothing was built on Windows.

audits.area: Rust build tool tools/pocket (toolchain discovery, Ninja generation, dependency fetch/CMake foreign builds, process spawning, watch, pack, run/test/editor/mcp, bootstrap) on a native Windows host
audits.current_platform_design:
The tool is 6,437 lines of Rust in 17 files (wc -l tools/pocket/src/*.rs). There is no Platform abstraction and no cfg(windows) anywhere. Platform handling uses three kinds of string seam.

(1) Target strings "native" | "wasm" | "ios-sim" (toolchain.rs:18-19, manifest.rs:316-319). "native" means whatever the host is, so host and target are conflated for desktop.

(2) Host checks on std::env::consts::OS inline in the generator: `tc.host_os == "macos"` for -mmacosx-version-min (ninja.rs:41-45), `host_os == "linux"` for gnu17 (ninja.rs:54) and for an lld link rule with --start-group plus -ldl -lpthread -lm (ninja.rs:63-68).

(3) A generic per-host override table on [[dependencies]]: keys "{os}-{arch}" then "{os}" (manifest.rs:141-143), with Apple frameworks dropped off macOS (manifest.rs:169-173) and pkg-config for Linux system deps (manifest.rs:174-186). Target overrides "ios-sim"/"ios" go through Workspace::for_target (manifest.rs:296-306).

The dependency seam is the cleanest part. On Windows, std::env::consts gives "windows-x86_64" and "windows" keys, so [dependencies.platforms.windows] tables work with zero tool changes.

POSIX assumptions are spread thinly but in many places:
- The ar rule is `rm -f $out && $ar rcs` (ninja.rs:60). Ninja on Windows passes the command string straight to CreateProcess, with no shell.
- Archives are named lib{name}.a (ninja.rs:102,118). Executables have no .exe (ninja.rs:112, commands.rs:138-142, pack.rs:102).
- which() does dir.join(name).is_file() with no .exe/PATHEXT (toolchain.rs:93-102). On Windows it finds no clang++, ninja, cmake, cargo or python3, and ar falls back to the literal "ar" (toolchain.rs:177).
- "python3" is hard-coded (commands.rs:42,1063; pack.rs:459,614).
- The pack launcher is a #!/bin/sh script (pack.rs:108-110).
- The diagnostics parser splits on ':' (report.rs:61-75), so a C:\ drive letter breaks it.
- std::fs::canonicalize is used at 16 call sites (check.rs, commands.rs, watch.rs, ts.rs). On Windows it returns \\?\ verbatim paths that leak into tsconfig globs, runtime arguments and project.json.

Unix-only APIs are already cfg-gated (deps.rs:155-159, pack.rs:41-47 and 65-68). The Cargo.lock already has winapi-util, windows-sys and windows-link, and every crate is pure Rust or supports Windows. By inspection the tool should compile for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc as is; I did not build it, because the audit was read-only.

Already portable:
- MCP over stdio, and the runtime control client over a raw TcpStream (mcp.rs:568-582)
- The file watcher, which polls mtimes (watch.rs:19-85, 172-203)
- Archive extraction in-process with tar, flate2, lzma-rs and zip (deps.rs:138-186)
- curl for downloads (deps.rs:113), which ships with Windows 10 1803+

Overall the seams are moderately clean. The Linux port needed only 92 changed lines in the tool (commit 49fd3360: manifest.rs +79, ninja.rs +13). The iOS Simulator target needed 381 (commit 4e71010b). Windows is a host port, not just a new target, so it touches paths, process spawning and file naming as well as flags. It is still a bounded change, roughly 1.5 to 3 times the iOS one.

work_items.item: Windows toolchain discovery and doctor checks
work_items.where: tools/pocket/src/toolchain.rs:93-102 (which), 174-196 (detect), 177 (ar fallback); commands.rs:29-45 (doctor)
work_items.why: Today `pocket build` fails at once on Windows: which("clang++") never matches clang++.exe, and ar falls back to the literal "ar". Changes: make which() try .exe and PATHEXT. Find clang++ on PATH, else in %ProgramFiles%\LLVM\bin, else in VS's bundled LLVM via vswhere. Use llvm-lib (or llvm-ar) as the archiver. Require `clang++ -dumpmachine` to end in windows-msvc, so an MSYS2/mingw clang cannot mix ABIs with the MSVC wgpu library. Record `clang++ -print-runtime-dir` for the ASan DLL. In doctor, check vswhere (%ProgramFiles(x86)%\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe) and the Windows SDK registry key (reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Kits\Installed Roots /v KitsRoot10) so errors are clear. Clang and lld-link find MSVC and the SDK by themselves, so the tool only needs to verify and report, not pass -libpath flags.
work_items.risk: medium: Windows installs vary (LLVM from llvm.org, LLVM bundled with VS, VS Build Tools only, no VS at all); auto-detection exists in clang and in lld-link (LLVM 15+) but has to be exercised on a real machine

work_items.item: Windows branch of the Ninja generator
work_items.where: tools/pocket/src/ninja.rs:54-68 (rules), 102/118 (lib names), 112 (exe name), 73-75 and 130-132 (unquoted -I and lib paths); commands.rs:138-142 (exe_path)
work_items.why: The ar rule `rm -f $out && $ar rcs` (ninja.rs:60) cannot run, because Ninja hands the string to CreateProcess with no shell. Replace it with `llvm-lib /nologo /out:$out $in`, which always writes a fresh archive. The link rule becomes `$cxx -fuse-ld=lld $ldflags -o $out $in $libs -Wl,-nodefaultlib:libcmt`; lld-link resolves archives in any order, so no --start-group is needed. Add the .exe suffix: the probe shows `-o pocket_runtime` becomes `-out:pocket_runtime` with no .exe, so Ninja's target name and pack's copy (pack.rs:101-103) must name the .exe. Name libraries .lib. Add Windows compile defines and flags, hard-coded the way the Linux branch is: -fms-runtime-lib=dll, NOMINMAX, WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN, _CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS (the CRT deprecation warnings would otherwise fail -Werror). Quote -I and lib paths; checkout paths with spaces are common on Windows. Response files are not needed: the longest ar/link line in build/release/build.ninja is 2,713 characters (measured 2026-10-02), against CreateProcess's 32,767.
work_items.risk: medium: the current flags compile for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (probe in the notes). But the C runtime choice only shows its effect at a real link: with -fms-runtime-lib=dll the objects carry /DEFAULTLIB:msvcrt while the driver still adds -defaultlib:libcmt, and the Rust-built wgpu_native.lib uses the dynamic CRT by default.

work_items.item: Path normalisation: dunce::canonicalize and one canonical workspace root
work_items.where: canonicalize sites: check.rs:37,41,54,120; commands.rs:149,411,417,418,591,597; watch.rs:97-99; ts.rs:288,293,479; also main.rs:259-281, ts.rs:570-579 (module_id), docs.rs:64; Cargo.toml (add dunce)
work_items.why:
On Windows, std::fs::canonicalize returns \\?\ paths, and the Rust docs say only backslash-delimited paths can be joined to them. Today those paths would reach:
- tsconfig include globs `{dir}/**/*.ts` and paths (check.rs:61-64, 80-81)
- the runtime's --project argument (commands.rs:149)
- project.json `dir` (commands.rs:597)
- the bundle's lines.json source (ts.rs:560)

module_id strips a non-canonical sdk_dir (commands.rs:590) from canonical paths, so SDK modules lose their pocket/ ids. watch.rs:99 builds a '/' prefix from display(), which prints backslashes. Windows paths also compare case-sensitively in strip_prefix. The fix: canonicalize ws.root once with dunce in workspace_root, use dunce at every site, and normalise '\\' to '/' where paths become ids or messages.
work_items.risk: low: mechanical, and covered by the existing ts.rs and commands.rs unit tests

work_items.item: Compiler diagnostics parser that handles drive letters
work_items.where: tools/pocket/src/report.rs:61-75
work_items.why: Builds use -fdiagnostics-absolute-paths (ninja.rs:46), so clang prints C:\...\file.cpp:10:5: error: .... Splitting on ':' (splitn(4, ':')) yields file "C", so `pocket build --json` reports no diagnostics. Agents rely on these. Strip a leading drive prefix before splitting, and add a unit test.
work_items.risk: low

work_items.item: CMake foreign builds configured for clang targeting MSVC
work_items.where: tools/pocket/src/deps.rs:229-272
work_items.why: With -G Ninja on Windows, CMake searches for cl.exe unless told otherwise. Outside a VS developer prompt it fails; inside one it builds the deps with cl. For native builds on Windows, pass -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER/-DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER (tc.cc/tc.cxx) and an explicit -DCMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY=MultiThreadedDLL. That is CMake's release default, and it must match the engine's -fms-runtime-lib=dll; otherwise MSVC STL's RuntimeLibrary detect_mismatch fails the link. Also pass llvm-rc/llvm-ar if CMake asks. Deps are always built Release (deps.rs:238), so _ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL stays consistent with the engine's non-debug CRT.
work_items.risk: medium: SDL3, libwebp, draco, freetype and harfbuzz each still have to configure and build with clang targeting MSVC; draco and harfbuzz are the most likely to need extra cmake_args

work_items.item: Windows tables in pocket.toml
work_items.where: pocket.toml:73-213 (all dependencies), especially :85 (sdl3 link_flags -lpthread -lm), :92-103 (wgpu), :165-185 (typescript), :203-213 (javascriptcore)
work_items.why:
No Windows host table exists. Needed:
- sdl3: libs = ["lib/SDL3-static.lib"]. SDL names its static library SDL3-static when the suffix is .lib (SDL CMakeLists.txt:3744, release-3.4.16). Link flags: kernel32 user32 gdi32 winmm imm32 ole32 oleaut32 version uuid advapi32 setupapi shell32 (CMakeLists.txt:2390). The base -lpthread -lm must be overridden, since pthread.lib and m.lib do not exist on MSVC.
- wgpu: url wgpu-windows-x86_64-msvc-release.zip (v29.0.1.1 release, 2026-06-23), libs lib/wgpu_native.lib (static, so no wgpu_native.dll to ship), link flags d3dcompiler ws2_32 userenv bcrypt ntdll opengl32 (wgpu-native v29.0.1.1 examples/framework/CMakeLists.txt).
- libwebp, draco, freetype, harfbuzz: .lib names, confirmed on the first build.
- typescript: @typescript/typescript-win32-x64 7.0.2 (published 2026-07-08); sha256 to compute on first fetch, because npm publishes sha512 only.
- javascriptcore: kind = "skip" on Windows, and a V8 entry from the script-engine work (ADR 0005).
- Also update the doc comment at manifest.rs:112-115.
work_items.risk: low to medium: data only, but the V8 entry depends on the script-backend work, which is outside this area

work_items.where: tools/pocket/src/check.rs:25
work_items.why: The checker is found at prefix/lib/tsc. The Windows package ships lib/tsc.exe (unpkg listing of @typescript/typescript-win32-x64@7.0.2, checked 2026-10-02), so `pocket check` and the `types` part of `pocket test` would report it missing.

work_items.item: Python discovery helper
work_items.where: tools/pocket/src/commands.rs:42 (doctor fontTools), 1063-1065 (python tests in pocket test); pack.rs:459 (font subsetting), 611-614 (Emscripten file_packager)
work_items.why: The python.org install manager provides python, py and pymanager. Its docs describe the python3 command only as a catch for accidental POSIX usage that is "not meant to be widely used". Look for python3, then python, then `py -3`, in one helper.
work_items.risk: low

work_items.item: Runtime launch environment (ASan DLL) for run, test, editor, scenario, bench, watch and mcp
work_items.where: commands.rs:174, 568-575 (runtime_command), 742, 925, 964; watch.rs:144-151; mcp.rs:251-277
work_items.why: debug is the default config for run, test and editor (main.rs:59,68,122,204), and it builds with -fsanitize=address,undefined (pocket.toml:20-24). On the MSVC target the probe shows clang links clang_rt.asan_dynamic plus the static runtime thunk. The resulting exe therefore needs the clang_rt.asan_dynamic DLL from `clang++ -print-runtime-dir` on PATH, or copied beside it; otherwise every debug test fails to start. Add the directory to PATH in one helper that every spawn site uses. LeakSanitizer does not exist on Windows; the Linux port had already turned leak checking off.
work_items.risk: medium: UBSan coverage alongside ASan on Windows has not been verified at run time; the fallback is a Windows-only debug config with ASan alone

work_items.item: Native pack for Windows
work_items.where: tools/pocket/src/pack.rs:82-123 (pack), 40-49 (set_executable), 108-111 (launcher, README)
work_items.why:
Changes:
- Copy bin/pocket_runtime.exe.
- Write <name>.cmd as the launcher: "%~dp0bin\pocket_runtime.exe" --project "%~dp0project" --bundle "%~dp0project.js" --project-config "%~dp0project.json" %*. The current one is a #!/bin/sh script.
- Ship the dynamic CRT DLLs app-local (vcruntime140.dll, vcruntime140_1.dll, msvcp140.dll, from the VS redist folder found through vswhere), or document that the VC++ Redistributable is required. The UCRT is part of Windows 10+.
- Ship the ASan DLL when packing a debug config; the macOS CI does `pack assets --config debug` (.github/workflows/ci.yml).
- Fix the README text.
- Optionally use the GUI subsystem for shipped games; keep the console for development, because run, test and mcp read the runtime's stdout JSON.

wgpu and V8 are static, so there are no other DLLs.
work_items.risk: medium: finding the redist directory, and the redistribution terms, need the owner's decision

work_items.item: Line endings: .gitattributes (or normalise in gen)
work_items.where: repository root (no .gitattributes exists); tools/pocket/src/gen.rs:658-669 (write_if_changed), 693-697 (--check); commands.rs:82 (gen runs on every build)
work_items.why: Git for Windows commonly checks out with core.autocrlf=true, which turns files into CRLF. gen.rs compares CRLF files with LF content, so every `pocket build` would rewrite the 7 generated files. That gives them new mtimes and recompiles engine/world each time, and `pocket gen --check` always fails. .editorconfig asks for lf but does not control Git. Fix with `* text=auto eol=lf` in .gitattributes, or CRLF-insensitive comparison in gen.rs.
work_items.risk: low

work_items.item: Windows bootstrap and the tool path in agent configs
work_items.where: scripts/bootstrap.sh:1-15 (POSIX sh, macOS only); .mcp.json ("command": "./.pocket/pocket"); .codex/config.toml (untracked); commands.rs:412 (project guide path .pocket/pocket)
work_items.why:
Add scripts/bootstrap.ps1. It should:
- check prerequisites: rustup, LLVM 21+, VS Build Tools with the Windows SDK, cmake, ninja, python
- run cargo build --release
- copy pocket.exe into .pocket\. A running pocket.exe (for example an MCP server) is locked on Windows, so rename the old file first, then copy.
- run pocket setup and pocket doctor

The project guide written for new projects and the MCP configs should name .pocket\pocket.exe, or be verified to resolve the extensionless path.
work_items.risk: low

work_items.item: Unit tests for the Windows-specific logic
work_items.where: tools/pocket/src/{report,toolchain,ninja,ts}.rs #[cfg(test)]
work_items.why: Cover drive-letter diagnostics, which() with PATHEXT, \\?\ path normalisation, and a build.ninja snapshot for a forced Windows host. These can run on macOS, so most regressions are caught without a Windows machine.
work_items.risk: low

work_items.item: First end-to-end run on a Windows machine, and fixing what it finds
work_items.where: whole tool; pocket setup/doctor/build/test/run hello/editor/pack/mcp
work_items.why: I could only probe flags by cross-targeting from macOS: a trivial source, no MSVC STL or Windows SDK headers, no link. The real link (CRT mix, ASan DLL), the CMake dep builds, tsc.exe and pack all have to be run once on Windows.
work_items.risk: high: this is first contact, and turnaround is slower if the only Windows machine is remote or a VM

work_items.item: Documentation: Windows sections and the driver decision
work_items.where: docs/build-system.md:139-140, 279; docs/decisions/0001-tech-stack.md:24, 37
work_items.why: The docs plan clang-cl. I recommend the GNU-style clang++ driver targeting x86_64-pc-windows-msvc instead: it produces the same MSVC-ABI objects and keeps the whole flag set and the gcc depfiles. clang-cl would need a second flag dialect (/I /D /Fo, deps = msvc), and its -MD means "dynamic CRT", not "write a depfile". This deserves an ADR note, plus a Windows prerequisites section.
work_items.risk: low

work_items.item: (Optional) Web builds from a Windows host
work_items.where: tools/pocket/src/toolchain.rs:64 (HOME), 69, 129, 139-140 (em++, emcc, emar)
work_items.why: The emsdk lookup uses HOME, which is usually unset on Windows (USERPROFILE is). It also launches the extensionless em++/emcc/emar files, which are POSIX launchers; on Windows the .bat wrappers must be used.
work_items.risk: low

work_items.item: (Optional) Pinned LLVM fetch in pocket setup, as docs/build-system.md:139 plans
work_items.where: tools/pocket/src/deps.rs:164-170 (xz decoded fully into memory), toolchain.rs
work_items.why: LLVM 23.1.2 (2026-09-22) publishes clang+llvm-23.1.2-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.tar.xz. But extract() decodes a whole .tar.xz into a Vec before untarring, so a multi-GB toolchain archive needs streaming decompression first. Not needed if developers install LLVM themselves.
work_items.risk: medium

work_items.item: (Optional) Windows CI job
work_items.where: .github/workflows/ci.yml (macos-15 only today)
work_items.why: ADR 0001:37 plans windows-2025 with clang-cl. Per the owner's current practice CI is disabled and tests run locally, so this is optional.

blockers_or_permissions: A Windows machine the owner provides: an x64 PC, or Windows 11 on Arm in a VM on the Mac. The ARM route builds aarch64-pc-windows-msvc. wgpu-native v29.0.1.1 ships wgpu-windows-aarch64-msvc-release.zip, npm has @typescript/typescript-win32-arm64 7.0.2, and LLVM 23.1.2 ships aarch64-pc-windows-msvc tarballs. From macOS I can only cross-probe compiler flags, not link or run.

Visual Studio Build Tools (MSVC libraries and Windows SDK) are under Microsoft's license terms, which the owner must accept. Using Build Tools requires a valid Visual Studio license; Community is free only within its eligibility terms. Since 2022-08-18 the terms also allow compiling OSI-licensed C++ dependencies without one (https://devblogs.microsoft.com/cppblog/updates-to-visual-studio-build-tools-license-for-c-and-cpp-open-source-projects/). Rust's x86_64-pc-windows-msvc host toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml channel 1.98.1) needs the same Build Tools.

Installing LLVM 21+ (llvm.org MSI or tarball; 23.1.2 is current, 2026-09-22), CMake, Ninja (v1.13.2 has ninja-win.zip and ninja-winarm64.zip) and Python on Windows. Machine-wide installers may need administrator rights, which only the owner can grant.

Long paths: the dependency builds under .pocket\build\<dep>-<ver>\... can approach MAX_PATH (260). Enabling LongPathsEnabled is a system setting only the owner can change. The alternative is a short ASCII checkout path such as C:\dev\aipocket, which also avoids spaces and non-ASCII characters in paths that Ninja and CMake pass along.

Distributing the VC++ runtime DLLs app-local inside packs, or requiring the VC++ Redistributable, is an owner decision under Microsoft's redistribution terms. Code signing for packed games (SmartScreen) needs a paid certificate; it is optional.

Outside this area, but needed before `pocket run` can execute scripts on Windows: a V8 prebuilt monolith (ADR 0005:34). JavaScriptCore has no Windows system framework. The tool's only part is a pocket.toml dependency entry; the build recipe and ABI choices (V8's bundled libc++ versus the MSVC STL) belong to the script-backend work.
audits.notes:
BOTTOM LINE FOR THE BUILD TOOL
The Rust tool's Windows port is small and mechanical, not an architectural change: about 470 to 1,040 changed lines across the required items (about 300 to 650 of them Rust, the rest TOML, PowerShell, docs and tests), and about 2.5 to 7.5 focused agent-days, most likely 3 to 4. The single largest uncertainty is the first real Windows link: C runtime choice, ASan DLL, and CMake builds of five dependencies with clang targeting MSVC. Nothing in the tool's design needs to change; everything slots into its existing seams:
- per-host [dependencies.platforms.windows] tables
- an inline host branch in ninja.rs like the Linux one
- one exe/lib suffix rule
- a which() fix
- dunce for paths
The engine's own Windows platform layer and the V8 backend are separate items, and V8 dominates their cost.

WHAT THE ESTIMATE RESTS ON
- Measured precedent in git. The Linux port changed 92 lines of the tool (49fd3360: manifest.rs +79, ninja.rs +13). The iOS Simulator target changed 381 tool lines (4e71010b: pack 137, ios 72, toolchain 52, manifest 47, main 30, deps 26, ninja 11, commands 4, graph 2). Both were committed on 2026-10-01, about two hours apart, which shows agent velocity on this codebase.
- Windows is a host port, so it additionally touches paths (16 canonicalize sites), process spawning (python3 at 4 sites, which()), file naming (.exe, .lib) and the shell-free Ninja command semantics. Hence the 1.5 to 3 times iOS scale.
- The day figures assume an agent works directly on a Windows machine. A remote or VM-only machine pushes toward the high bound.

PROBES I RAN (scratchpad only; Apple clang 21.0.0, --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, trivial source, no repo files touched)
- The current flag set compiles to a COFF object and writes a Makefile depfile, so `deps = gcc` keeps working: -std=c++26 -fvisibility=hidden -ffp-contract=off -fdiagnostics-absolute-paths -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O0 -g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -MD -MF.
- -fsanitize=address,undefined compiles, and the link (-###) uses lld-link with clang_rt.asan_dynamic.lib plus -wholearchive clang_rt.asan_static_runtime_thunk.lib. A debug exe therefore needs the ASan DLL at run time.
- -luser32 becomes user32.lib, so pocket.toml link_flags can stay in -l form.
- `-o pocket_runtime` is passed as -out:pocket_runtime, so the generator must add .exe itself.
- -fms-runtime-lib=dll puts /DEFAULTLIB:msvcrt.lib into objects and defines _MT and _DLL, but the driver's link line still adds -defaultlib:libcmt. Hence the -Wl,-nodefaultlib:libcmt in the link-rule item.
- Not probed: MSVC STL and Windows SDK headers under C++26 with -Werror (engine area), and any real link.

OTHER CHECKS
- No symlinks in any cached dependency archive (tar -tv on .pocket/cache: SDL3, draco, libwebp, basisu, freetype, harfbuzz, typescript all 0), so Windows Developer Mode is not needed for extraction.
- The runtime control server binds 127.0.0.1 only (engine/app/src/server.cpp:169,171), so `pocket run --watch` and MCP sessions should not trigger a Windows Firewall prompt.
- The longest ar/link line in build/release/build.ninja is 2,713 characters, so response files are not needed.

CROSS-AREA ITEMS FOUND IN PASSING (not counted above)
- The runtime's --exit-with-parent uses getppid (engine/app/src/runtime.cpp:229), which has no Windows equivalent. Implement it in the engine by waiting on the parent's process handle, or have the tool put the child in a kill-on-close Job Object (mcp.rs:251-277, which would add the windows-sys crate).
- The agent benchmark runners use os.killpg (tools/scripts/runners/opencode_agent.py:93,97; pi_agent.py:112,116), which does not exist on Windows. They also hard-code .pocket/pocket (agent_eval.py:31, opencode_agent.py:46, pi_agent.py:49). agent_eval.py:4203 runs with shell=True.
- docs/build-system.md:11 says libc++ everywhere. On Windows the practical library is the MSVC STL. LLVM's Windows releases do not ship libc++ for MSVC.

WORKING TREE STATE (read-only; nothing edited, built or committed)
The aipocket working tree has untracked rust-toolchain.toml (channel 1.98.1), .codex/ and docs/development.md, and modified .gitignore and tools/scripts/agent_eval.py, apparently from concurrent work. I left build/agent-traces and build/eval-runtime untouched.

audits.area: Engine C++ on Windows: the platform layer audited for clang targeting the MSVC ABI with the MSVC STL (engine/**/src, engine/**/include and tests/**, third_party excluded)
audits.current_platform_design:
The platform layer is thin, and most of it is clean. Two libraries carry nearly all of the OS work. SDL3 handles windows, input, IME, clipboard, gamepads and audio, and only pocket_platform and pocket_audio use it (engine/platform/module.toml, engine/audio/module.toml). wgpu-native handles the GPU: the engine asks for one optional feature, TimestampQuery (engine/rhi/src/device.cpp:393), and the renderer also runs in browsers.

Scripts reach the engine only through the 14-method ScriptHost interface (engine/script/include/pocket/script/script_host.hpp:32-60). core/fs reads and writes in binary mode (engine/core/src/fs.cpp:9,17,36). Threading is plain std::thread, mutex and condition_variable, with no pthread (engine/core/src/parallel.cpp:27-140). There is no file watching in the engine; `pocket watch` lives in the Rust tool. Paths that agents see are already relative and use generic_string(), at 19 sites (for example engine/assets/src/assets.cpp:2136, 2355, 2405, 2425 and engine/app/src/session.cpp:6495, 6646). The importers strip `\r` (engine/assets/src/import.cpp:73, 147, 317).

Size: across engine and tests there are 84,446 lines of C++ (third_party excluded) and 62 platform conditionals in 15 files. About 1,600 lines sit inside platform branches. Of those, about 435 are web-only (web_host.cpp 205, web_fs.cpp 42, server_web.cpp 16, plus branches in runtime, net, device and platform), about 341 are the JavaScriptCore host, and only about 160-180 lines call POSIX, Apple or Linux OS APIs. That last group is:
- BSD sockets: 32 lines in engine/app/src/net.cpp.
- Two copies of posix_spawn plus waitpid: engine/app/src/session.cpp:7002-7019 and engine/assets/src/import.cpp:584-597.
- getppid and SIGHUP: engine/app/src/runtime.cpp:227-237.
- Native window handles: engine/platform/src/platform.cpp:180-266.
- WebGPU surfaces: engine/rhi/src/device.cpp:318-347.
- Blender install paths: engine/assets/src/import.cpp:485-498.

The existing `_WIN32` checks are 7 lines, and every one switches a feature off rather than implementing it (session.cpp:31, 6990; import.cpp:21, 576; runtime.cpp:16, 227, 232).

Where the seams are not clean:
- There is no OS-services layer. posix_spawn is duplicated in two modules.
- Sockets are written inline in the lockstep protocol code, held in `int` (net.cpp:54, 119) and checked against errno.
- `#ifndef __EMSCRIPTEN__` is used to mean "POSIX" (net.cpp:36, server.cpp:1, jsc_host.cpp:1). On Windows those branches therefore pick POSIX code.

What breaks today on Windows:
- **Will not compile:** net.cpp includes <arpa/inet.h>, <poll.h>, <sys/socket.h> and <unistd.h> (net.cpp:36-47). jsc_host.cpp needs JavaScriptCore headers (jsc_host.cpp:7).
- **Compiles but fails or is disabled:**
  - Windowed runs: the Linux branch is the fallback, so they fail with window_handles_missing (platform.cpp:259-265). Headless runs work.
  - `project.apply`, the agent's main edit loop: returns "unsupported" (session.cpp:6990-6992).
  - Blender import: returns "unsupported" (import.cpp:576-577).
  - `--exit-with-parent` does nothing (runtime.cpp:231-237), although `pocket mcp` starts every runtime with it (tools/pocket/src/mcp.rs:252-253).

C++ library use is conservative. The code uses <expected> (core/result.hpp:8), 134 std::format calls, 9 std::print/println calls (core/src/log.cpp, app/src/runtime.cpp), <numbers>, <span>, 3 std::bit_cast and one integer std::from_chars (session.cpp:4131). It uses no ranges or views, flat_map, inplace_vector, stacktrace, <execution>, mdspan, char8_t, long double or __builtin_. It has one __attribute__ (core/src/log.cpp:147), and its #pragma clang diagnostic lines only wrap third-party headers. The MSVC STL provides everything used: microsoft/STL yvals_core.h on main defines __cpp_lib_format at line 1715, __cpp_lib_expected at 1771 and __cpp_lib_print at 1787.

The engine already builds against two standard libraries. libc++ is used on macOS and the web. libstdc++ 15 is used on Linux, and that port changed only about 78 engine lines in 8 files, one of them a missing #include (commit 49fd3360, 2026-10-01).

work_items.item: Port lockstep networking to Winsock behind a small socket layer
work_items.where: engine/app/src/net.cpp:36-47 (POSIX includes; <poll.h> is unused), 54 and 119 (sockets held in int and compared with < 0), 96-111 (fcntl O_NONBLOCK, TCP_NODELAY), 192, 464, 488 and 514-517 (::close), 331 and 386 (recv/send with ssize_t and errno EAGAIN), 540-553 (socket, bind, listen, getsockname), 620-634 (getaddrinfo, connect)

The new layer needs: a socket_t type with INVALID_SOCKET, closesocket, ioctlsocket(FIONBIO), WSAGetLastError and WSAEWOULDBLOCK, one WSAStartup call, error text from system_category, and const char* optval for setsockopt. It should also set SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE instead of SO_REUSEADDR (net.cpp:543): on Windows, SO_REUSEADDR lets a second socket hijack the port (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winsock/using-so-reuseaddr-and-so-exclusiveaddruse, page dated 2018-05-31, updated 2025-03-11). On Windows, connecting to a closed localhost port only fails after SYN retries of a few seconds (daniel.haxx.se/blog/2024/08/14/slow-tcp-connect-on-windows/, 2024-08-14), so the join retry loop at net.cpp:623-633 gets slower. audits.notes:
To your question (backends 迁移的代码复杂吗？): no, the engine's own platform code is small and well bounded. Developing natively on Windows still needs real work, mostly OS services (sockets, process launching, process lifecycle), UTF-8 paths and a script backend.

**Totals for engine C++ alone** (excluding the script backend, the Rust build tool and dependency fetching):
- About 400-870 new or changed lines.
- About 5-12 focused agent-days.
- The script backend adds 20-80 lines and about 1-3 days with Bun's JavaScriptCore build, or 500-800 lines and about 4-8 days with V8 (plus hours to build the V8 artifact).

**Suggested order:**
1. Headless build and tests: build settings, UTF-8 manifest, Winsock (or a temporary stub), compile fallout, .gitattributes, script backend.
2. Window and editor: HWND surface, backend choice, precise sleep.
3. Agent benchmark: process API for project.apply, --exit-with-parent, plus the Rust MCP and build-tool work covered in other audits.
4. Cross-play: lockstep determinism check between macOS and Windows.

**What the numbers rest on:**
- **Calibration:** the Linux port changed about 78 engine lines in 8 files and was done in about a day (git 49fd3360, 2026-10-01). Linux was POSIX with JavaScriptCore available; Windows is not POSIX and has no JavaScriptCore.
- **Counts behind the line estimates:** the exact sites cited per item: 32 BSD socket lines, 2 spawn blocks, 271 path .string() calls, 18 getenv and 5 strerror calls, 8 near/far/small collisions.
- **Typical sizes:** about 60-90 lines for a Winsock shim, about 90-120 for a CreateProcessW runner with quoting, and about 25-40 for an HWND surface.
- **Days** assume an agent working on a Windows box where Visual Studio Build Tools and Clang already work and the build tool already emits Windows builds. The high bounds are mostly first-run test triage and determinism checks.

**Recommendations:**
- Compile with `clang++ --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, not clang-cl. docs/build-system.md:139 and :279 plan clang-cl; the reasons to revisit that are in the first work item.
- Add an `engine/core` OS layer (process run, parent watch, precise sleep, sockets) so windows.h stays in one or two translation units.
- Prefer the Vulkan backend, matching Linux.
- Ship the UTF-8 manifest before anything else. On a Chinese-locale Windows, any project or user path with Chinese characters otherwise crashes JSON output.

**Lower-risk items checked and found fine:** std::thread-based parallel_for; binary file I/O; agent-visible paths already use generic_string; CRLF handled in the OBJ, MTL and PLY importers; no ABI-sensitive layouts (alignas(16) uniforms with static_asserts, renderer.cpp:173 and 272); no `long` or LLP64 problems; no std random distributions in the simulation; loopback-only control server through cpp-httplib, which supports Windows and links ws2_32 itself (httplib.h:280).

**Not covered here:** packaged games (/SUBSYSTEM:WINDOWS with SDL_main, which today is included only for iOS, main.cpp:7-11), DPI behaviour on scaled displays, and the Rust tool, CMake foreign builds and Python scripts.

audits.area: Script host (engine/script: ScriptHost interface, JavaScriptCore backend, web host) on native Windows
audits.current_platform_design:
The seam is clean and narrow. engine/script/include/pocket/script/script_host.hpp:32-60 is a 14-method virtual interface (evaluate, bind, bind_numbers, share_f32/f64/u32/u8, call, has_function, drain_microtasks, collect_garbage, describe), and Config (:19-24) holds two fields: `inspectable` and `console_text`. Its only consumer is engine/app/src/session.cpp: it creates the host at :648-652 and makes 29 `host_->` calls, 9 of them drain_microtasks. No other module includes an engine header (ADR 0005:26-29, AGENTS.md:81). The backend is chosen at compile time, not from pocket.toml: jsc_host.cpp:1 is `#ifndef __EMSCRIPTEN__` and web_host.cpp:5 is `#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__`, and each defines ScriptHost::create (jsc_host.cpp:338-340, web_host.cpp:206-208). The runtime switch ADR 0005:34-36 promises for V8 does not exist.

The JSC backend (engine/script/src/jsc_host.cpp) is 343 lines, 300 of them code. It calls 41 distinct functions, all from the public JSC C API headers (JSBase, JSContextRef, JSObjectRef, JSValueRef, JSStringRef, JSTypedArray):
- Typed-array sharing: JSObjectMakeTypedArrayWithBytesNoCopy with a null deallocator (:321-329), so no memory is freed across the boundary.
- Protection from the collector: JSValueProtect on the __pocket object (:215) and on every call argument held in a heap vector (:276-288).
- Exceptions with stacks: the backend reads `stack`, `line` and `sourceURL` from the thrown object (:46-64).
- Modules: none. The bundle goes through JSEvaluateScript (:237-244), and ADR 0005:48-50 notes the C API has no module loader.
- Microtasks: JSC drains them when the outermost API call releases the JSLock, and the backend forces that by evaluating `void 0` (:300-305).
- Inspector: only JSGlobalContextSetInspectable (:212), which serves Safari on macOS.
- Natives: JSClass callAsFunction trampolines with private data, for JSON natives, number natives and console (:112-203).

The web host (web_host.cpp, 211 lines) marshals everything as JSON through EM_JS.

Dependencies (pocket.toml:73-214) describe macOS in their base fields. They are specialised by `[dependencies.platforms.<key>]` overrides. The host key is `<os>-<arch>`, then `<os>`, taken from std::env::consts (manifest.rs:112-117, 139-142, 268), and the target key is ios-sim, then ios (manifest.rs:295-305). An override can replace kind/url/sha256/cmake_args/libs/link_flags/defines (manifest.rs:121-136, 150-168). Frameworks are dropped off Apple (manifest.rs:169-173), and pkg-config feeds Linux system packages (manifest.rs:174-186). Because of this, `windows-x86_64`, `windows-aarch64` and `windows` keys work today with no schema change. None exist yet.

Kinds are handled in deps.rs:209-275:
- prebuilt: download with curl (deps.rs:113), check sha256, extract zip/tgz/txz in Rust.
- file: copied as is.
- cmake: `cmake -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` (deps.rs:237-272). Only wasm (emsdk) and iOS (deps.rs:239-249) have their own branch, so there is no Windows compiler, MSVC environment or CRT handling.

- The Ninja rules use GNU-driver syntax: `-MD -MF` (ninja.rs:57-59), `rm -f && ar rcs` (ninja.rs:60) and `lib*.a` names (ninja.rs:102).
- toolchain::which has no .exe/PATHEXT (toolchain.rs:93-101).
- check.rs:25 expects `lib/tsc`.

Python tooling is mostly portable because 26 scripts go through tools/scripts/dev/runtime.py. The Unix-only spots are concentrated in:

work_items.where: pocket.toml:10-30 (toolchain/configs), tools/pocket/src/manifest.rs (per-host config override), commands.rs test/run (ASan DLL dir on PATH)
work_items.why:
Configs are host-agnostic, and debug forces -fsanitize=address,undefined (pocket.toml:20-24). Windows needs:

- dbghelp.lib for flecs: under clang, ECS_TARGET_MSVC is undefined, so its #pragma comment(lib) is skipped (flecs.h:652-655, flecs.c:18741-18746).

audits.area: Windows development via WSL2, reusing the existing Linux support instead of a native Windows port
audits.current_platform_design:
The platform seams are narrow and clean. Inside WSL2 the build tool cannot tell it is not on ordinary Linux.

Build tool (tools/pocket):
- Host differences live in data. Each dependency has `[dependencies.platforms.<os>-<arch>]` or `<os>` tables (pocket.toml:110-116 for the wgpu-native Linux aarch64 and x86_64 zips, :175-181 for the TypeScript Linux tarballs, :210-213 for JavaScriptCore via `pkg_config = ["javascriptcoregtk-4.1"]`).
- These tables are resolved with `std::env::consts::OS/ARCH` (tools/pocket/src/manifest.rs:268). pkg-config is run at manifest.rs:174-180.
- Toolchain detection is clang on PATH, with POCKET_CXX/CC/AR overrides (toolchain.rs:174-197).
- The Linux-specific Ninja rules are `gnu17` and `lld` with `--start-group` (ninja.rs:53-68).
- WSL2 reports `linux`/`x86_64`, so all of this applies unchanged. Nothing in the tool checks for WSL.

Engine:
- **Window seam.** All window code is in engine/platform/src/platform.cpp:240-266. Emscripten, Apple and "else" branches each take SDL3's X11 or Wayland handles; it fails with `window_handles_missing` only when neither exists (:265).
- **GPU-surface seam.** Metal layer, Wayland surface or Xlib window, in engine/rhi/src/device.cpp:318-348.
- **Scripts.** They run on the JavaScriptCore C API with no Apple-only code (engine/script/src/jsc_host.cpp:1-7). On Linux this is WebKitGTK's JSC.
- **Audio.** SDL3, which degrades to silence when there is no device (engine/audio/src/audio.cpp:645-665).
- **Existing Windows guards.** `_WIN32` guards already stub out posix_spawn and getppid uses (engine/app/src/session.cpp:6990-6992, engine/assets/src/import.cpp:576-577, engine/app/src/runtime.cpp:16,227-236). They have never been compiled.
- **Control server.** It binds 127.0.0.1 (engine/app/src/server.cpp:169-171).
- **Architecture-specific code.** There is none in engine/ (no `__x86_64__`, `__aarch64__` or NEON/SSE intrinsics outside third_party). FMA contraction is off on every target (pocket.toml:13-16).

Size of the Linux port, for calibration:
- Commit 49fd3360 (2026-10-01 15:18) was 224 insertions in 13 files. About 60 of those lines are engine code (platform 23, device 20, headers 17). The rest is the manifest/pkg-config (79), Ninja (13), Dockerfile (15) and linux.sh (31).
- Commit b2bcd85c (17:07 the same day) added 74 lines for teardown and docs.

How Linux runs today:

- aarch64 release run: 23 of 24 test modules passed (build-system.md:225-227).
- x86_64 has only run under QEMU: about 9 hours, with runtime_tests failing and an inconclusive rerun (docs/development.md:166, an uncommitted file in the working tree).

blockers_or_permissions: A Windows 10 (fully updated) or Windows 11 machine of the owner's. Enabling WSL and running `wsl --install Ubuntu-26.04` needs admin/UAC. Ubuntu 24.04+ images use WSL's tar format, which needs WSL 2.4.10 or later (ubuntu.com/wsl install doc, read 2026-10-02).
A current Windows GPU driver; GPU paravirtualization comes from the Windows driver. NVIDIA says to install no Linux display driver inside WSL (CUDA on WSL guide v13.3, 2026-05-21).
The sudo password inside WSL for apt (the owner creates the Linux user on first launch). Per the user's standing rule, ask for anything needing sudo.
Raising memory and swap in %UserProfile%\.wslconfig if debug+ASan tests are wanted (more than 20 GB). This is a VM setting change, so it is the owner's decision; otherwise test with --config release.
The benchmark's model accounts and keys (DeepSeek for oh-my-pi, the Z.ai GLM coding plan for opencode) copied into the WSL environment. Paid accounts, owner-only.

Optional: usbipd-win (MSI, admin) to pass a gamepad into WSL. USB devices are not natively available in WSL (learn.microsoft.com connect-usb, updated 2026-06-02). The WSL kernel's HID gamepad support is unverified.
Optional: Linux Blender (blender_level task and .blend import) and a Linux Chrome .deb (web_offline.py). Free, but large downloads.
No licence acceptance is needed on this path. A native port would need the Windows SDK or VS Build Tools terms (or xwin), which docs/development.md:18 reserves for the owner.

Docker is not needed. Running linux.sh unchanged inside WSL would need a Docker engine, and Docker Desktop has commercial licence terms. Its container would also be headless only, with no WSLg socket or /dev/dxg.
audits.notes:
VERDICT
WSL2 with Ubuntu 26.04 runs the existing Linux build with close to zero porting.

The core path is items 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7. That is about 50-580 new or changed lines and 2-6.75 focused agent-days, almost all of it verification. Hardware-accelerated rendering (item 4) is extra: 0-400 lines and 1-4 days, with a real chance it ends in "stay on CPU rendering".

What the numbers rest on:
- The Linux port itself was 224+74 lines, landed in about two hours of commits on 2026-10-01 (49fd3360 at 15:18, b2bcd85c at 17:07). About 60 of those lines are engine code.
- WSL is that same target: the tool resolves `linux-x86_64` from std::env::consts (manifest.rs:268).
- Most of the range is unknown test failures on first real x86_64 hardware, plus the GPU-backend question.
- Wall-clock time for test suites and benchmark runs is not counted.

WHAT A WINDOWS USER GETS
- **Build and tests.** Builds of the tool, engine, debug and release, and `pocket test`. The release suite was 23/24 green on aarch64 in the container; x86_64 is still unproven (development.md:166).
- **Headless use.** Headless runs, captures, scenarios, the JSON-RPC control server and `pocket mcp`. A Windows-side agent can reach them through localhost forwarding or `wsl.exe`.
- **TypeScript tooling.** `pocket ts`, `pocket check` and `--watch`. The watcher polls mtimes (watch.rs:18-40), so it even works on /mnt/c, but keep the clone in ext4 for speed (learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/filesystems, updated 2026-06-02).
- **The agent benchmark.** It works with opencode and oh-my-pi on Linux.
- **The web build.** Emscripten runs in WSL and the result opens in a Windows browser.
- **Editor and windowed runs.** These work through WSLg: Weston and XWayland, audio through WSLg's PulseAudio server (github.com/microsoft/wslg README, read 2026-10-02). SDL3 is built against libpulse (Dockerfile:11), and audio falls back to silence if the device is missing (audio.cpp:645-665).

Caveats on the editor:
- Rendering is on the CPU (lavapipe, which Khronos lists as Vulkan 1.3 conformant: phoronix.com/news/Lavapipe-Vulkan-1.3-Official). Frame rate on heavy samples is unmeasured.
- Cursor lock and mouse-look are broken in WSLg (microsoft/wslg#376, opened 2021-07-21, still open).
- Windowed Linux has never been run, so the first run may find small issues.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO
1. **A native .exe for players.** `pocket pack` in WSL produces a Linux pack with a sh launcher (pack.rs:109). It needs libjavascriptcoregtk and a Vulkan driver on the target (docs/packaging.md:28-31). Windows players get only the web build.
2. **D3D12 timings or representative GPU performance.** WSL offers either the CPU (lavapipe), or OpenGL translated to D3D12 by Mesa's d3d12 driver, through wgpu's second-tier GL backend.
   - wgpu's DX12 backend is never exercised (WGPUInstanceBackend_DX12 in the pinned wgpu.h:801).
   - dzn, Vulkan over D3D12, is absent from Ubuntu 26.04's packages (packages.ubuntu.com, 2026-10-02) and hidden by wgpu as non-conformant (wgpu.h:850-861).
   - Vendor paths in WSL are CUDA, DirectX and DirectML only. NVIDIA's WSL guide does not mention Vulkan, and says OpenGL-CUDA interop is unsupported (docs.nvidia.com CUDA on WSL guide v13.3, 2026-05-21).
   - So gpu_probe.py numbers from WSL say nothing about Windows players.
3. **Catching Windows-specific bugs.** Code not exercised:
   - the `_WIN32` branches (session.cpp:6990-6992, import.cpp:576-577, runtime.cpp:16,227-236)
   - BSD sockets in net.cpp:549
   - posix_spawn
   - HWND surfaces (missing in device.cpp:318-348 and platform.cpp:240-266)
   - WASAPI audio, XInput/GameInput gamepads, drive letters and backslashes, case-insensitive paths, CRLF
   - clang-cl/MSVC ABI
   - the script engine: Windows has no system JavaScriptCore, and ADR 0005:34 plans V8 there.
   ADR 0001's windows-2025 CI (0001-tech-stack.md:37) stays unbuilt.
4. **iOS work.** That stays on the Mac.

GPU FINDING (the one real engineering point)
- device.cpp:303 creates the instance with defaults: all backends, including GL (wgpu-native v29.0.1.1 Cargo.toml default features, read 2026-10-02), and no environment overrides (wgpu-native src/lib.rs `new_without_display_handle`; docs.rs wgpu-types 29.0.1).
- wgpu-core sorts adapters Discrete < Integrated < Other < Virtual < Cpu (docs.rs wgpu-core 29.0.1). wgpu-hal labels a GL renderer 'D3D12 (NVIDIA ...)' as Other and 'D3D12 (Intel ...)' as Integrated (docs.rs wgpu-hal 29.0.1 gles/adapter.rs).
- So on a WSL box where Mesa's d3d12 GL works, the engine probably picks GL over lavapipe. That path is untested and would break the backend assertion at runtime_tests.cpp:136.
- This is inferred from source, not measured. The adapter log line at device.cpp:428 settles it on the first run.
- Item 3 makes the choice explicit. GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe is the zero-code way to reproduce the container's behaviour.
- Other WSL GPU background:
  - MESA_D3D12_DEFAULT_ADAPTER_NAME selects the GPU; the default is the integrated one (github.com/microsoft/wslg/wiki/GPU-selection-in-WSLg).
  - On 24.04, users report GL stuck on llvmpipe until they install kisak Mesa and set GALLIUM_DRIVER=d3d12 (forums.developer.nvidia.com topic 347383, 2025-10-11/18).
  - dzn reached about 99.86% of the Vulkan 1.2 CTS but was never certified (phoronix.com/news/Microsoft-Dzn-Vulkan-1.2). SDL ranked it above lavapipe for WSL on 2026-01-31 while saying it probably will never be conformance-tested (discourse.libsdl.org SDL commit e803c).

DISTRO CHOICE
- Use Ubuntu-26.04. It is installable on WSL (ubuntu.com/wsl/docs/stable/howto/install-ubuntu-wsl2, read 2026-10-02) and matches Dockerfile:4.
- Ubuntu 24.04 has neither clang-21 nor libstdc++-15-dev in its archive; questing and resolute do (packages.ubuntu.com, 2026-10-02). It would need apt.llvm.org plus a toolchain PPA.
- The engine only uses <expected> and <print> from newer libraries, which libstdc++ 14 has, so 24.04 would probably work, but it is untested.
- ADR 0001 names ubuntu-24.04 for CI (0001-tech-stack.md:37), which no longer matches the 26.04 container.

CAVEATS
- docs/development.md, rust-toolchain.toml and agent_eval.py:1270-1272 are uncommitted working-tree changes from a concurrent session (git status on 2026-10-02). Their line numbers may move.
- Nothing was built, run or edited. build/agent-traces and build/eval-runtime were not touched.
- Every behavioural claim about WSL is from documentation or source, not measured on a Windows machine. The first real WSL session should record:
  - the adapter and backend line (device.cpp:428)
  - the release suite result
  - editor FPS on a heavy sample.

plan.complexity_verdict:
Mostly clean, with a few tangled spots. Porting means wide but shallow work, not a redesign. I re-checked the cited sites at HEAD edbfe1b1; the audits started at 60b757ee, and the line numbers still match unless noted.

CLEAN
- **OS work goes through two libraries.** SDL3 handles windows, input and audio, and only pocket_platform and pocket_audio link it (engine/platform/module.toml, engine/audio/module.toml). wgpu-native handles the GPU (engine/rhi/module.toml).
- **Scripts sit behind one small interface.** ScriptHost has 14 methods (engine/script/include/pocket/script/script_host.hpp:32-60). The session creates it once (engine/app/src/session.cpp:651), and the only native backend is 343 lines (engine/script/src/jsc_host.cpp).
- **Dependencies already accept a Windows host.** The build tool picks per-host tables by std::env::consts (tools/pocket/src/manifest.rs:268), so `windows-x86_64` and `windows` tables work with no schema change. The Linux JSC table at pocket.toml:211-213 is the model.
- **The OS-specific code is small.** Engine and tests hold 84,446 lines of C++, with 62 platform conditionals in 14 files. Only about 160-180 lines call POSIX, Apple or Linux APIs.
- **Past ports were small.** Linux took 224 inserted lines in 13 files, 78 of them in engine/ (git 49fd3360). The iOS Simulator took 629 lines in 22 files, 381 of them in the tool (4e71010b). Both landed on 2026-10-01.

TANGLED
- **There is no OS-services layer.** posix_spawn is copied twice (session.cpp:7007-7013, engine/assets/src/import.cpp:587-594). BSD sockets are written inline in the lockstep code (engine/app/src/net.cpp:36-47, 543-546).
- **`#ifndef __EMSCRIPTEN__` is used to mean "POSIX".** See net.cpp:36 and jsc_host.cpp:1. The window code's `#else` assumes X11 or Wayland (engine/platform/src/platform.cpp:247, 259-265). A Windows build therefore lands in POSIX code paths.
- **The existing Windows guards only switch features off.** All 7 `_WIN32` lines do this, and none has ever been compiled (runtime.cpp:16, 227, 232; session.cpp:31, 6990; import.cpp:21, 576).
- **The build tool assumes a Unix host.** It has no cfg(windows). Host checks are inline strings (tools/pocket/src/ninja.rs:41-45, 54, 63-68). The archive rule needs a shell (`rm -f $out && $ar rcs`, ninja.rs:60), and Ninja on Windows has none. which() ignores .exe (toolchain.rs:93-101). python3 is hard-coded at 4 sites (commands.rs:42, 1063; pack.rs:459, 614). canonicalize is called at 16 sites. The diagnostics parser splits on ':' (report.rs:64), which breaks on C:\.
- **Configs ignore the host.** Debug forces -fsanitize=address,undefined on every host (pocket.toml:20-24), and the "native" target treats host and target as the same thing.

Bottom line: the backend migration code itself is not complex. The Windows cost comes from many small POSIX assumptions, a script engine Windows does not ship, and a first build on a machine nobody has used yet.

phases.name: 0. Decide and de-risk on the Mac (no Windows hardware needed)
phases.contents:
- **Bun JavaScriptCore spike** (20-40 lines, 0.5-1 d). On a throwaway branch, link oven-sh/WebKit's bun-webkit-macos-arm64 release lane plus mimalloc 3.2.8 instead of the system framework (pocket.toml:203-209). Then run pocket test, tests/ts, the editor and a few benchmark tasks. jsc_host.cpp uses only the public JSC C API (jsc_host.cpp:7), but Bun's CI never exercises that path on Windows (audit 3: oven-sh/WebKit lanes.mjs:36-39, read 2026-10-02).
- **ADR amendment and Windows docs** (80-180 lines, 0.3-0.8 d). Four decisions:
  - Compiler: `clang++ --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` with lld, not the clang-cl that docs/build-system.md:139-140 and :282 plan. Under clang-cl, -Wall means -Weverything and -MD means "DLL CRT", while our flags in pocket.toml:10-24 and ninja.rs:57-60 are GNU-style. Audits 1, 2 and 4 agree.
  - Script engine: JSC from Bun, or V8 as ADR 0005:34 says.
  - C runtime: dynamic (/MD), with JSC behind a DLL.
  - GPU: Vulkan first.
- **.gitattributes** with `* text=auto eol=lf` plus binary patterns (5-15 lines, 0.05 d). None exists. Under core.autocrlf, gen.rs would rewrite its 7 generated files on every build and `pocket gen --check` would always fail. Audits 1, 2 and 4 all raised this; it is counted once.
phases.done_when: macOS `pocket test` and tests/ts pass against Bun's JSC. If they do not, the spike's list of C-API breakages switches the plan to V8 before any Windows work. The owner has accepted the decisions.

phases.name: 1. pocket and the engine libraries build on Windows
phases.contents:
- **Toolchain discovery and doctor** (90-170 lines). Teach which() .exe and PATHEXT (toolchain.rs:93-101). Find clang++ on PATH, in %ProgramFiles%\LLVM, or in VS's LLVM via vswhere. Use llvm-lib instead of the literal "ar" fallback (toolchain.rs:176). Require `-dumpmachine` to end in windows-msvc. Have doctor check vswhere and the SDK registry key (commands.rs:29-45).
- **Ninja Windows branch, flags and per-host config** (70-150 lines). Merges audit 1 (35-70), audit 2 (20-40) and audit 4 (50-110).
  - Archive with llvm-lib instead of the shell rule at ninja.rs:60.
  - Link with `-fuse-ld=lld -Wl,-nodefaultlib:libcmt` and no --start-group (ninja.rs:63-68).
  - Name outputs .exe and .lib (ninja.rs:102, 112, 118; commands.rs:138-142), and quote paths.
  - Defines: NOMINMAX, WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN, _CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS, _CRT_NONSTDC_NO_DEPRECATE, _WIN32_WINNT=0x0A00. Also -fms-runtime-lib=dll and dbghelp for flecs.
  - A per-host config override so arm64 drops ASan (pocket.toml:20-24).
- **Path handling** (25-50 lines). Use dunce at the 16 canonicalize sites, keep one canonical workspace root, and turn '\\' into '/' wherever a path becomes an id.
- **Diagnostics parser** (15-35 lines). Handle drive letters (report.rs:64).
- **CMake dependency builds** (20-80 lines; deps.rs:229-272). Pass explicit compilers, CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY=MultiThreadedDLL and llvm-rc. The audits disagree here: audit 1 says clang and lld-link find MSVC by themselves, while audit 4 says the vcvars environment must be captured. The range covers both.
- **Windows tables in pocket.toml** (45-80 lines, data only).
  - sdl3: SDL3-static.lib plus the Win32 system libraries, overriding -lpthread and -lm.
  - wgpu: the v29.0.1.1 windows-x86_64-msvc and aarch64-msvc zips (digests in audit 4).
  - libwebp, draco, freetype, harfbuzz: .lib names.
  - typescript: the win32 packages.
- **Programs the tool runs** (20-45 lines). Look for lib/tsc.exe (check.rs:25). Add one Python lookup helper for the 4 python3 sites. Set PYTHONUTF8=1 for the Python it starts.
- **ASan runtime DLL** (15-30 lines). Put its directory on PATH in one helper that every spawn site uses (run, test, editor, watch, mcp).
- **Application manifest** (25-60 lines). Embed activeCodePage=UTF-8 and longPathAware in the runtime and test executables. Without it, a Chinese path on a code-page-936 machine makes nlohmann dump() throw (audit 2).
- **MSVC STL fallout** (0-40 lines). It is the third standard library after libc++ and libstdc++.
- **Explicit GPU backend choice** (20-60 lines). wgpuCreateInstance(nullptr) at device.cpp:303 enables every backend. Add WGPUInstanceExtras with a POCKET_GPU_BACKEND override, put Vulkan first, and report the adapter. Audits 2, 4 and 5 each proposed this; it is counted once, and WSL needs the same change.
- **scripts/bootstrap.ps1** (35-70 lines). Copy pocket.exe by renaming the old file first, because Windows locks a running exe. Name .pocket\pocket.exe in .mcp.json and in the project guide (commands.rs:412).
- **Unit tests that run on macOS** (40-90 lines). Cover drive letters, PATHEXT, \\?\ paths, and a build.ninja snapshot for a forced Windows host.
- **First-contact fixes** (50-150 lines). The first real link will show the CRT mix, the ASan DLL and the five CMake dependencies built by clang for MSVC.

phases.name: 2. Scripts and the headless runtime (samples/hello)
phases.contents:
Scripts come before the window, not after as the suggested order had it. The session always creates a ScriptHost (session.cpp:651), and runtime_tests asserts that the engine is JavaScriptCore (tests/runtime_tests/runtime_tests.cpp:138). net.cpp, which is part of pocket_app, also does not compile today.

- **Winsock socket layer** (90-150 lines). Replace the POSIX includes (net.cpp:36-47). Add socket_t, INVALID_SOCKET, closesocket, ioctlsocket and WSAGetLastError. Use SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE instead of SO_REUSEADDR (net.cpp:543). Call WSAStartup once and link ws2_32.
- **JSC Windows tables** (35-60 lines). Point the javascriptcore entry at Bun's pinned release lane (pocket.toml:203-213), add mimalloc 3.2.8 as a CMake dependency, and add a `version` field to DependencyOverride (manifest.rs:121-166).
- **jsc_host.cpp include and version fixes** (5-20 lines). Add explicit includes for the MSVC STL, and have engine_version() report the pinned WebKit commit.
- **pocket_jsc.dll** (120-300 lines). Link it with lld-link /DLL and a .def that exports the C API, generate the import library, and copy the DLL next to the executables. This settles the audits' C runtime conflict: Bun's JSC is built with the static CRT (/MT, audit 3), while wgpu's Rust staticlib and CMake's defaults use the dynamic CRT (/MD, audits 1 and 4). It also links the roughly 35-45 MB JSC once instead of into 4 executables (an inferred size), and it is the relinkable form the LGPL requires for shipping. Cheaper fallback for bring-up: build the engine with /MT and link wgpu as its DLL.
- **Runtime lifecycle** (30-80 lines). --exit-with-parent does nothing on Windows (runtime.cpp:227-236), yet `pocket mcp` passes it to every runtime it starts (mcp.rs:252-253). Wait on the parent's process handle, use SetConsoleCtrlHandler to set g_stop, and optionally put children in a kill-on-close Job Object.
- **windows.h macros** (5-25 lines). httplib pulls windows.h into runtime_tests, where its near, far and small macros break local names. Keep windows.h inside the new OS translation units.
- **save.list time** (3-8 lines). session.cpp:5653-5654 uses time_since_epoch, and the MSVC file_clock counts from 1601.
- **Script parity** (0-60 lines). Fix version differences between Apple's JSC and Bun's fork, including tests/ts/repro.test.ts.
phases.done_when: `pocket run samples/hello` headless writes a report with script.engine JavaScriptCore. runtime_tests, audio_tests and renderer_tests pass in release. `pocket mcp` starts a runtime that exits when the tool does.

- **HWND surface** (25-40 lines). Add a `_WIN32` branch that reads SDL_PROP_WINDOW_WIN32_HWND_POINTER and the instance pointer (platform.cpp:259-265, which today fails with window_handles_missing). Create a WGPUSurfaceSourceWindowsHWND in device.cpp:318-347, with new fields in platform.hpp and device.hpp.
- **Precise sleeps** (10-25 lines). The MSVC STL's sleep_for ends in Sleep(ms). Use SDL_DelayPrecise for frame pacing and network waits in session.cpp and net.cpp.

It covers DPI scaling, IME for Chinese input, present modes, editor frame rate, pixel tolerances on a real GPU, and the firewall prompt the first time --net-host binds INADDR_ANY (net.cpp:546).

- **First full run of the 405 test cases** (20-100 lines), in debug (ASan and UBSan under the MSVC ABI) and release. It covers the backend assertions (runtime_tests.cpp:133-137), about 45 text-mode test writes that produce CRLF, and the golden hash (tests/evidence/hello-golden.json) on x86-64 with the MSVC STL.
- **`pocket pack` for Windows** (60-130 lines). Merges audits 1 and 4.

  - Ship the VC++ runtime DLLs next to the exe, or document that the Redistributable is required.

- **Cross-machine lockstep check** (0-40 lines). Host on macOS arm64 with a Windows x64 peer. The risky spots are 54 unstable std::sort calls, 22 unordered containers and 22 std:: transcendental calls in simulation code (audit 2 counts).
- **suite.sh replacement** (25-50 lines). Replace tools/scripts/dev/suite.sh (nohup sh -c) with a Python runner that works on both hosts.
phases.done_when: `pocket test` passes in debug and release, or has only triaged and documented skips. MCP project_apply works. `pocket pack` produces a folder that runs on a clean Windows install. A macOS-Windows arena session stays in sync.

phases.name: 5. Agent benchmark on Windows
phases.contents:
- **Benchmark runners** (60-120 lines).
  - Replace start_new_session plus os.killpg(SIGKILL) (opencode_agent.py:89-97, pi_agent.py:108-116) with a shared helper that kills the process tree through a Job Object.
  - Use .exe paths.
  - Use forward slashes in paths shown to agents, whose shell is Git Bash.
  - Pass multi-line prompts through stdin or a file, because cmd.exe shims cut argv at the first newline.
- **Harness and SDK** (15-40 lines). Add .exe to the POCKET path (tools/scripts/agent_eval.py:31), tools/scripts/dev/runtime.py and sdk/python/pocket_env.py. Fix the Blender task's path and the shell=True runner string.
- **Smoke run** (0-50 lines; my estimate). Install the Windows builds of opencode and oh-my-pi plus Git for Windows, run a smoke test, and fix what it finds. Wall-clock time for full benchmark runs is not counted.
phases.done_when: agent_eval's reference runner and one opencode (GLM) run finish on Windows. Their traces are comparable with macOS, and no runtime outlives its task.

biggest_risks: Nothing has been built on Windows yet. Audit 1 checked by reading that the tool compiles; audit 2's MSVC STL claims come from STL source. The C runtime mix (wgpu's Rust staticlib on /MD, Bun's JSC on /MT), ASan with UBSan under the MSVC ABI, and five CMake dependencies built by clang for MSVC only show up at the first real link. This drives the high bounds of phases 1 and 2.

The script engine. Bun's JSC runs in production inside Bun on Windows x64 and arm64, but its CI never tests the C-API path we use. Each architecture is a 385 MB autobuild from a third party under LGPL-2+. If the macOS spike fails, V8 replaces the JSC items: about 560-1,100 lines and 5-12 days instead of 180-480 lines and 2.5-5.75 days, so roughly +380-620 lines and +2.5-6 days net, plus multi-hour V8 builds per attempt and per architecture.

x86-64 has never run on real hardware. Under QEMU, runtime_tests failed and the rerun was inconclusive (docs/development.md:316). The MSVC STL brings a third std::sort and a third set of unordered containers, so the golden state hash and lockstep determinism with macOS may diverge.

The GPU path. Vulkan needs a vendor driver; VMs and some Windows-on-Arm machines may only offer DX12 or WARP, which pulls in DXC or the slow FXC for the 133 KB WGSL module at renderer.cpp:529. Pixel tolerances may need retuning on new drivers.

Unicode paths. On a zh-CN Windows (code page 936), the 271 path .string() calls and nlohmann's strict dump() fail on Chinese paths unless the UTF-8 activeCodePage manifest ships first. That manifest needs Windows 10 1903 or later.

Iteration speed and drift. Days assume an agent working directly on the Windows machine; a remote or VM-only box pushes toward the high bound. CI is disabled, so macOS-side changes will keep breaking Windows unless it gets periodic local runs.
The benchmark on Windows. Job Objects with Bun and Node agent process trees, Git Bash path quoting and .cmd shims need a live check with each agent.

plan.wsl2_path:
**Cost (audit 5).** Running the existing Linux build in WSL2 with Ubuntu 26.04 takes about 50-580 new or changed lines and 2-6.75 agent-days. Almost all of it is verification:
- a WSL host recipe (30-120 lines)
- the first run on real x86_64 hardware, plus fixes (0-250)
- explicit GPU backend selection (20-60)
- the first windowed Linux run through WSLg (0-80)
- the benchmark inside WSL (0-40)
- a web build from WSL (0-30)

Hardware-accelerated rendering is optional: 0-400 lines and 1-4 days, with a real chance the answer is "stay on CPU rendering". The tool resolves linux-x86_64 from std::env::consts (manifest.rs:268) and has no WSL checks.

**Setup facts:**
- Ubuntu 26.04 matches the container (tools/docker/linux/Dockerfile:4). Ubuntu 24.04's archive lacks clang-21 and libstdc++-15.
- Clone into the Linux filesystem, not /mnt/c.
- Debug with ASan needs more than 20 GB of VM memory, so raise .wslconfig or test with --config release.
- No Microsoft licence acceptance and no Docker are needed.

**What it gives:**
- tool, engine, debug and release builds, and `pocket test`
- headless runs, captures, the control server and `pocket mcp`
- the TypeScript tooling and watch mode
- the agent benchmark (opencode itself recommends WSL on Windows)
- the web build, opened in a Windows browser
- the editor and windowed runs through WSLg, on CPU rendering (lavapipe)

**What it does not give:**
- a Windows .exe for players: `pocket pack` makes a Linux pack with an sh launcher (pack.rs:108-110), so Windows players get only the web build
- representative GPU or D3D12 performance: rendering is CPU lavapipe, or GL over D3D12 through wgpu's second-tier backend, and Ubuntu does not package dzn
- a working cursor lock or mouse-look in WSLg (microsoft/wslg#376, open since 2021-07-21)
- any coverage of Windows-specific code: Winsock, CreateProcess, HWND, MSVC ABI and STL, drive letters, CRLF, and the script engine

**What carries over to a native port.** The backend-selection change and the first real x86-64 run, about 20-310 lines and 0.75-3.25 days, are needed natively anyway.

**One finding to settle on the first run.** device.cpp:303 enables every wgpu backend, so on WSL with a working Mesa d3d12 driver the engine may choose GL over lavapipe. That would break runtime_tests.cpp:136. This is inferred from wgpu source, not measured. GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe is the zero-code workaround.
owner_actions: Provide a Windows machine: an x64 PC running Windows 10 1903+ or 11 with a GPU that has a current Vulkan/D3D12 driver. A Windows 11 on Arm VM on the Mac can build and run headless, but likely has no hardware GPU (inference). An Arm PC is needed only to verify windows-aarch64. From the Mac I can only cross-check compiler flags, not link or run.

Community is free only within its eligibility terms; commercial use beyond them needs a paid Visual Studio licence. Accept the LGPL obligations for shipping JSC: a DLL plus a notice and relink instructions. Mirror the pinned Bun WebKit archives, about 385 MB each, under your GitHub account. Decide whether packs ship the VC++ runtime DLLs next to the exe or require the VC++ Redistributable.

For the WSL2 path instead: enable WSL and run `wsl --install Ubuntu-26.04` (admin/UAC, WSL 2.4.10+), create the Linux user and give the sudo password for apt, and decide whether to raise VM memory above 20 GB in %UserProfile%\.wslconfig for debug+ASan.
plan.recommendation:
Is the backend migration code complex? No. The OS code sits behind SDL3, wgpu and a 14-method ScriptHost. Only about 160-180 of 84,446 C++ lines call POSIX, Apple or Linux APIs, and the build tool's dependency tables already accept Windows keys.

How much a native Windows port adds: about 1,230-2,970 new or changed lines and 12.5-33 focused agent-days, across six phases that each end in something runnable.
- My judgement of the likely outcome is about 1,700-2,000 lines and 16-20 days. The high bound assumes every first-contact fix hits its upper end.
- The numbers rest on two measured precedents: the Linux port (224 lines in 49fd3360) and the iOS target (629 lines in 4e71010b), both landed in a day.
- They also rest on per-site counts and on the sizes of comparable code (jsc_host.cpp is 343 lines).
- They exclude wall-clock build, download and benchmark time.

Suggested order:
1. **Run the Bun JavaScriptCore spike on the Mac first** (0.5-1 day, no Windows needed). It decides whether the script engine costs about 3-6 days (JSC) or an extra 2.5-6 days plus multi-hour builds (V8).
2. **If the goal is simply to develop on a Windows PC, use WSL2 with Ubuntu 26.04.** It covers build, tests, MCP, the editor on CPU rendering and the benchmark, for about 2-7 agent-days, mostly verification, with no Microsoft licence. Its backend-selection change and first real x86-64 run carry over to a native port.
3. **Go native only when you need one of these:**
   - a Windows .exe for players
   - real Windows GPU performance
   - coverage of Windows-only bugs

   Then follow phases 1-5:
   - Compile with clang++ targeting MSVC, not clang-cl.
   - Put sockets, process launching, parent watching and precise sleep in one small pocket_core OS layer, so windows.h stays out of the rest of the engine.
   - Use Vulkan first.
   - Use the dynamic CRT, with JSC in its own DLL. That settles the CRT conflict between the audits and is the form the LGPL needs anyway.
   - Ship the UTF-8 manifest early, because Chinese-locale paths crash JSON output without it.
   - Budget periodic Windows runs, since CI is disabled.

Where the audits disagreed, I chose as follows:
- **C runtime:** audits 1 and 4 assumed the dynamic CRT, audit 3 the static one. Resolved by the JSC DLL.
- **CMake environment:** audit 1 says clang finds MSVC by itself, audit 4 says vcvars must be captured. The estimate range covers both.
- **Script engine:** audit 4 priced V8 into its totals; audit 3 recommends JSC. My totals use JSC, with V8 as the fallback.
- **Process API:** audit 2 estimated 150-230 lines, audit 4 80-160. I used 150-250 to include the test call sites.

Every Windows behaviour claim in the audits comes from reading source or documentation, not from a build.

review.verdict:
Somewhat too optimistic. The code map is accurate: I re-checked about 40 of the cited sites at HEAD edbfe1b1 and they hold, with two small slips listed under wrong_claims. The OS surface in the engine is genuinely small. In engine/ and tests/ the POSIX headers are included only in session.cpp:31-37, runtime.cpp:16-18, net.cpp:36-47 and import.cpp:21-27. Engine file I/O is binary-mode through core/fs.cpp:9-38, and IDs mostly use generic_string. The external artifacts the estimate relies on exist:
- wgpu-native v29.0.1.1 has windows-x86_64-msvc and aarch64-msvc zips (https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu-native/releases/tag/v29.0.1.1, published 2026-06-23, checked 2026-10-02).
- Bun's WebKit autobuild-4fde1587 has bun-webkit-windows-amd64.tar.gz at 385,206,749 bytes and windows-arm64 at 366,255,197 bytes (https://github.com/oven-sh/WebKit/releases/tag/autobuild-4fde158736b8393fc31be471cc2bbca1d826d42b, 2026-10-01).
- @typescript/typescript-win32-x64 and -arm64 7.0.2 are on npm (published 2026-07-08).
- LLVM 23.1.2 is the latest release (2026-09-22) and ships x86_64- and aarch64-pc-windows-msvc tarballs.
- The V8 fallback really is expensive. kuoruan/libv8's last release is v13.1.201.22 (2025-01-08), which is stale. rusty_v8 v152.2.0 (2026-08-20) uses Chromium's libc++ (ADR 0005:13-14).

Where it is optimistic:
1. **The Mac spike cannot de-risk the Windows script engine.**
   - The macOS lane links the system ICU (oven-sh/bun scripts/build/deps/webkit.ts:131).
   - The Windows lane is built by clang-cl with the static CRT (Dockerfile.windows:388). It bundles ICU whose data is zstd-compressed and read through a hook the embedder must define (Dockerfile.windows:229-243; jsc.cpp:211-267).
   - The fork's CI tests no Windows lane at all (lanes.mjs:36-39). Its build compiles only jsc and testFFI, not the C-API test program testapi (Dockerfile.windows:440).
   - Read at oven-sh/WebKit main on 2026-10-02.
2. **Missing items.** The estimate omits the web (wasm) build from a Windows host and the ICU hook. It also pins upstream mimalloc 3.2.8, while Bun links its fork, oven-sh/mimalloc eab09015.
3. **Debug sanitizers and the first full test run are sized as if they will go smoothly.**
   - Debug forces ASan+UBSan (pocket.toml:20-24) on top of /MD CMake dependencies and a /MT JSC.
   - The Linux debug runtime_tests needed more than 20 GB (docs/build-system.md:229-230).
   - Linux's first real run needed a 74-line renderer teardown fix (b2bcd85c).
   - x86_64 runtime_tests failed under QEMU and the failure was never diagnosed (docs/development.md, iOS and Linux section).
4. **The precedents are POSIX siblings.**
   - Linux was 224 lines (49fd3360) plus the 74-line follow-up, and it ran headless only.
   - iOS was 629 lines (4e71010b).
   - Both reused posix_spawn, BSD sockets, signals and a JSC that came with the system, so they say little about a port to a new ABI, CRT and script engine.

The estimate also overstates one risk. STL-driven drift in the golden hash already did not happen across libc++ and libstdc++: in the Linux arm64 release run, the only failure was the Metal assertion (docs/build-system.md:228-229). Native-to-wasm lockstep has already been checked with repro math and -ffp-contract=off (docs/design/networking.md:116-141).

Adjusted range:
- I add 2.5-8 agent-days and about 190-610 lines, giving roughly 1,420-3,580 lines and 15-41 days.
- The likely case is 20-25 days.
- As in the original, wall-clock time for builds, the suite and downloads is excluded, and on an unprepared Windows box it will dominate calendar time.
- If the JSC path fails on Windows itself, not just on the Mac, add the estimate's V8 fallback of 2.5-6 days.
missed_items: Web/wasm build from a Windows host is in no native phase. Emscripten is detected by checking for an `em++` file under HOME or EMSDK (tools/pocket/src/toolchain.rs:57-73). On Windows, emsdk installs em++.bat, emcc.bat and emar.bat, and HOME is usually unset (USERPROFILE). The archive rule's `rm -f` shell command is shared with emar (ninja.rs:60). .bat wrappers go through cmd.exe and its 8191-character command-line limit. tools/scripts/web_offline.py:24 hard-codes the macOS Chrome path. wasm_core_tests.py needs node. About +30-80 lines and +0.5-1.5 days.

ICU decompress hook for Bun's Windows JSC. The Windows lane bundles a static ICU whose data items are zstd frames. They are read through a weak `bun_icu_maybe_decompress` hook that the embedder must define (oven-sh/WebKit Dockerfile.windows:229-243; Source/JavaScriptCore/jsc.cpp:211-267, main, read 2026-10-02). Without it, the compressed items (locale and collation data) silently fail, which breaks Intl, localeCompare and toLocaleString in agent-written game scripts. The macOS lane uses the system ICU (oven-sh/bun scripts/build/deps/webkit.ts:131), so the Mac spike cannot catch this. The zstd decoder is already vendored (third_party/basisu/zstd/zstddeclib.c). About +40-80 lines and +0.25-0.5 days.

A first-day Windows-side JSC C-API smoke link is needed before investing in pocket_jsc.dll: about 30-60 lines covering JSGlobalContextCreateInGroup, JSObjectMakeTypedArrayWithBytesNoCopy, the microtask drain and JSGlobalContextSetInspectable against the 385 MB tarball. The fork's CI tests no Windows lane (lanes.mjs:36-39). Its Windows build compiles only the jsc and testFFI targets, not JSC's C-API test program testapi (Dockerfile.windows:440).

Debug sanitizer bring-up under the MSVC ABI is under-budgeted at 15-30 lines.
- pocket.toml:20-24 forces -fsanitize=address,undefined on top of non-ASan Release CMake dependencies (MSVC STL container-annotation consistency) and a /MT JSC.
- LLVM ships no Windows arm64 ASan runtime (oven-sh/WebKit lanes.mjs:156).
- Linux runtime_tests under sanitizers needed more than 20 GB (docs/build-system.md:229-230), so the phase 4 'passes in debug' target may be infeasible on a 16-32 GB PC.
- Decide early whether Windows debug drops ASan.
- About +10-60 lines and +0.5-2 days.

The first full test run is under-budgeted at 20-100 lines. Linux's first real run needed a 74-line teardown fix (b2bcd85c: renderer.cpp, device.cpp, renderer_tests). x86_64 runtime_tests failed under QEMU, undiagnosed (docs/development.md, iOS and Linux section). Windows adds the MSVC STL, a new JSC build, x86-64 and a real GPU at once. About +40-150 lines and +0.5-2 days.

The windowed renderer has never run on Vulkan with a real driver. Linux ran only headless on lavapipe, and windowed Linux has never run. That leaves the 133 KB WGSL module (renderer.cpp:529 onward) through naga to SPIR-V on NVIDIA/AMD drivers, first-launch pipeline compile time, and swapchain resize and occlusion with presented_frames pacing (session.cpp:6764-6774). About +0.25-1 day on phase 3.

Windows file locking. A running pocket_runtime.exe, or a loaded pocket_jsc.dll or ASan DLL, cannot be overwritten or deleted. The MCP server keeps runtimes alive (mcp.rs:252-253), and the editor and watch keep one open (watch.rs:144-151). So relinks, and `remove_dir_all` of dependency prefixes and build dirs (deps.rs:206-207, 232-234), fail while any runtime runs. The tool needs to detect this and stop runtimes or report it clearly. About +10-40 lines.

Packed Windows game entry point. pocket_runtime is a console-subsystem executable with a plain main (engine/runtime/src/main.cpp:13); SDL_main.h is included only for iOS (main.cpp:7-11). A player who double-clicks it gets a console window, and the .cmd launcher the estimate proposes opens one too. The fix is /SUBSYSTEM:WINDOWS through SDL_main or /ENTRY:mainCRTStartup, plus an llvm-rc icon and version resource. About +15-40 lines.

mimalloc pin. Bun links its fork oven-sh/mimalloc at commit eab09015 (2026-09-16), per oven-sh/bun scripts/build/deps/mimalloc.ts:15. That commit is 208 commits ahead of and 85 behind upstream dev3. Upstream 3.2.8 is not what the WebKit release lanes (USE_EXTERNAL_MIMALLOC=ON, lanes.mjs:238-239) were built and tested against.

Script debugging. `--inspectable` (runtime.cpp:37, jsc_host.cpp:212) relies on Safari's Web Inspector, which does not exist on Windows. Bun's JSC compiles the remote inspector in (ENABLE_REMOTE_INSPECTOR=ON, Dockerfile.windows:420), but there is no frontend bridge. Windows developers lose script debugging unless a WebSocket bridge is written, which is out of scope or about +150-400 lines.

Benchmark Python text encoding and paths. tools/scripts/agent_eval.py has 50 open() calls, none with encoding=. These decode with the ANSI code page (936 on zh-CN) unless PYTHONUTF8=1 or Python 3.15+ (PEP 686) is used, and that applies when the owner runs it directly, not only when the tool starts it. agent_eval.py:4178 replaces os.path.join(ROOT, 'docs'), which is backslashed on Windows, so the prompt rewrite silently becomes a no-op. About +10-30 lines.

Owner action not listed: a Windows Defender exclusion for the checkout (.pocket/, build/). Real-time scanning of the 385 MB JSC extraction, thousands of objects and ASan executables is a major iteration-speed cost on a fresh box, and adding the exclusion needs admin rights.
